reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing the pair, reread the dedicated current regulations, the outline and the current course list before comparing the decisions. Independently recomputed three 60 EC years, checked the study periods and dependencies of the nine illustrative electives and traced thesis preparation, internship and assessment separately. Reconsidered the actual current workbook evidence before confirming the repaired plans and reader content.
findings: The English full-time September 2026 standard pathway has no formal routes. The first year comprises eight courses, two skills courses and two projects at 5 EC each. Year two comprises four courses, two skills courses, two projects and four restricted electives at 5 EC each. Year three has one required course, one skills course, one project and five restricted electives at 5 EC each, plus 2.5 EC thesis preparation and 17.5 EC thesis research grouped as BENP2004 for 20 EC. The 45 EC of electives come from the official Business Engineering menu. The dated catalogue examples show a feasible academic selection across the listed elective periods. Artificial Intelligence and Data Science require first-year calculus and linear algebra. Financial Markets requires Corporate Finance and Investment, scheduled before it. The public record preserves the elective menu rather than claiming a selected route. The standard pathway includes local study and a thesis internship; optional exchange and approved outside replacements follow the dedicated EER.

The dedicated EER sets the BSA at 45 first-year EC without a named-course requirement. This standard sequence completes all 60 first-year EC before the final phase. Multivariable Calculus follows BENC1002. The core catalogue entries and elective examples were checked for credit, prerequisites and entry scope. The project and skills entries marked as not available exam-only require normal participation. Year-three thesis entry requires every first-year course, skill and project to be passed. Internship Office approval triggers registration. The 20 EC bundle includes an internship and an individual academic paper, presentation and defence. The Internship Office page gives a minimum three-month placement. Attendance and registration are conditions within the course credits. The programme-specific EER governs any optional exchange and limits a student to either study abroad or thesis research abroad.

The official catalogue supports restricted rather than open elective treatment. The thesis package combines two curricular allocations within a single 20 EC catalogue record, and the compulsory internship and defence are included. UCR’s materials and lab contribution is bounded but substantive, especially crystallography, stress and strain, material recovery and prototype practice. The first option preserves those strengths with sustainability systems and business. The second retains quantitative and computing depth while AI adoption and governance replaces a partner project that could not fit the available terms. Both plans meet current offerings and prerequisites. Their nine distinct courses each support their different questions, while shared business and mathematics connect them to the same comparator.
